task.name: A run records what it cost but not what it changed, so spend cannot be attributed to code
task.story_text:
## Why

A run's audit record says what the work cost and never says what it touched. The coordinator
already computes the file set — `review_git_context.diff_stat` carries a full per-file diffstat —
but it is emitted to the log stream and dropped, not persisted into the audit record.

The consequence is that spend cannot be attributed to code. Reconstructing the join after the fact
from git history collapses almost entirely:

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| commits scanned (`git log --all`) | 2,456 |
| commits naming more than one issue, so unattributable | 823 |
| issues with recorded cost in `audit_records` | 266 |
| issues joinable to a file set after the fact | **12** |
| spend inside that joinable sample | **$187 of $1,868 (10%)** |

Both halves exist. `audit_records` holds `total_cost_usd`, `complexity_score`, `outcome_success`,
`verdict` and `issue_id`; git holds the file changes; and 265 of the 266 cost-bearing issues appear
somewhere in commit history. What is missing is the edge between them. A third of commits reference
several issues, so commit-to-run attribution is ambiguous, and no amount of parsing recovers what
was never recorded.

Anything that asks "which parts of this codebase are expensive to change" is unanswerable until a
run records the files it changed. That includes ADR-0008's replacement for the withdrawn module-size
ratchet, which depends on ranking modules by observed cost rather than by line count.

This is worth doing on its own terms even if nothing consumes it soon: the data is already computed
and thrown away, capture is cheap, and every day without it is a day of unattributable spend. It
accrues value only going forward — no fix makes the last three months attributable.

## Example

`.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json` currently records cost with no file set:

```
"cost":    { "total_usd": 64.56, "dev_usd": 49.90, "review_usd": 14.08 },
"reviews": [ { "cycle": 1, "commit": "443d476b…", "verdict": "APPROVE" } ]
```

Wanted: the changed-file set as first-class data on the record, so cost and code can be joined
without parsing git or guessing at commit attribution:

```
"changed_files": {
  "base_ref": "0c92c4e9…",
  "head_ref": "4661b33b…",
  "files": [
    { "path": "src/theforge/process_group.py", "insertions": 540, "deletions": 312 },
    { "path": "src/theforge/process_tree.py",  "insertions": 505, "deletions": 0 },
    { "path": "tests/test_process_tree.py",    "insertions": 368, "deletions": 0 }
  ]
}
```

Two properties the shape has to hold. It must be recorded for runs that do not reach review — an
escalated or failed run still consumed money against files, and those are the runs most worth
attributing. And it must survive into the SQLite index in a form that can be queried per file
without loading and parsing every `raw_json` blob, since answering "what did this module cost" by
deserialising 1,084 records is the kind of query nobody runs twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A completed run's audit record contains the set of files the run changed against its base ref,
      with per-file insertions and deletions.
- [ ] The file set is recorded for runs that terminate before review, including escalated and failed
      runs.
- [ ] The recorded base and head refs identify the comparison the file set was derived from.
- [ ] The file set is queryable per file from the audit index without deserialising every record's
      `raw_json`.
- [ ] A query joining a file to the runs that changed it returns, for a known recent run, the same
      files that run's commits actually touched.
- [ ] Records written before this change remain readable, and their absent file set is distinguishable
      from an empty one.

handoff.summary: Added a structured changed-file capture to the run record. A new coordinator/changed_files.py resolves base/head to SHAs at capture time and parses git numstat between them (--no-renames so every entry is a real path; binary files flagged rather than recorded as 0-line changes). capture_changed_files stores the snapshot on CoordinatorState at the pre-cleanup seam inside land_story — both the local-merge branch (after the pre-merge auto-commit) and the merge-pr branch — because landing removes the worktree and deletes the branch. generate_audit_log serialises that snapshot as a top-level changed_files field, falling back to a transient (unstored) collection from a still-present worktree, which is what covers escalated and pre-review-failed runs; the fallback is deliberately not stored so the in-flight audit flush cannot freeze a mid-run answer. null (no comparison) and {files: []} (a comparison that found nothing) are kept distinct end to end. The block is projected into a new audit_changed_files SQLite table keyed (run_id, path) with an index on path and rewritten per-run on upsert; runs_touching_path() joins it to audit_records for per-file spend. Record schema bumped 27->28 with reader-side _migrate_v27_to_v28 backfilling null, and substrate schema 8->9 with _reindex_changed_files so already-indexed history carrying the block is backfilled on open. ADR-0002 documents the block, the SQL, and both bumps. Also fixed a pre-existing porcelain-parse bug in _parse_dirty_files that my landing test exposed.

story_deviations: The collector lives in a new module coordinator/changed_files.py rather than beside _get_diff_stat in review_context.py as the plan's Step 1 said. Both audit.py and completion.py need it, and neither should import review-context gathering to get it; review_context._get_diff_stat is untouched and still serves the review prompt.

Per-file entries carry a `binary` boolean in addition to path/insertions/deletions (and a `binary` column in the index). git reports `-`/`-` for binary files; coercing to a bare 0/0 would make a changed binary indistinguishable from a file with no line changes.

Fixed a pre-existing bug in coordinator/gate.py::_parse_dirty_files, in scope under the in_scope P2 policy because the pre-merge cleanup is exactly where the capture seam sits. _run_shell strips its combined output, so a first porcelain line of ' M path' arrived one column short and the fixed-offset slice produced 'ath'-style mangled paths; the pre-merge auto-commit then staged a nonexistent pathspec and dropped the file from the merge. The parser now detects the short prefix instead of assuming the column width.
deferred_items: The snapshot is not added to resume_persistence's serialized blocks. Capture happens in the same process that lands the story, and a resumed attempt re-captures from its own worktree, so a resumed run is covered; a snapshot taken in a prior process is not carried across the resume boundary.

The in-flight audit flush (write_live_story_audit) emits a freshly collected block each time rather than a frozen one. That is intentional — the story is not finished — but it means an in-flight audit.yaml's changed_files describes the moment it was flushed, not the run.

17 tests fail in this sandbox (test_cut_rc_isolation, test_sprint_lock, test_sprint_reexec_collision) with 'Operation not permitted' from mktemp and multiprocessing.synchronize. They fail identically in isolation, touch none of the modified code, and are environment restrictions rather than regressions; the authoritative gate runs outside the sandbox.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 names 'the successful landing paths' and 'escalated or failed terminal paths' but sprint/runner.py has many terminal writers — _write_story_audit is called from ~15 sites (runner.py:4015, 4092, 4170, 4195, 4267, 4331, 4360, 4366, 7002, 7098, 7202, 7228, 7345, 7437) and land_story is called once at runner.py:4298. Scattering capture calls across those sites risks missing one.
  Suggestion: Prefer a single capture entry point invoked once per run (e.g. an idempotent capture_changed_files(state, config) that no-ops if the snapshot is already set), called immediately before land_story at runner.py:4298 and once on the coordinator's terminal transition, rather than editing each _write_story_audit call site.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The new CoordinatorState field will not survive a resume: resume_persistence.py serializes explicit blocks (capture_phase_blocks, _preflight_block, _review_progress_block, …) rather than dataclasses.asdict, so an unregistered field is silently dropped.
  Suggestion: Capture within the same process that lands the story (which the plan already does), or add the snapshot to capture_phase_blocks/_merge_phase_blocks if a resumed run must retain a snapshot taken in the prior process.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 lists completion.py and runner.py as edit targets but not sprint/audit.py, where _write_story_audit and the in-flight flush call generate_audit_log (sprint/audit.py:1499 and :1636). The in-flight flush constructs a synthetic CoordinatorResult and will emit changed_files: null mid-run.
  Suggestion: Confirm the in-flight path intentionally emits null (the story is not finished), or note that the flush may capture opportunistically since its worktree still exists.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Binary file insertions/deletions are represented as '-' in git numstat output, which will cause ValueError if parsed directly using int().
  Suggestion: Handle '-' in git numstat parsing safely (e.g. coerce to 0 insertions/deletions or handle binary file structures explicitly).

plan_finding_registry.description: The approach captures changed_files in generate_audit_log() from the final workspace, but successful landing can delete that workspace before the terminal audit is generated. coordinator/workspace.py::_merge_branch removes the worktree after a local merge, and coordinator/completion.py::_step_cleanup removes it after merge-pr. sprint/runner.py::_attempt_integration calls land_story() before _write_story_audit(), so the final record will receive changed_files: null for a normal landed run. The optional CoordinatorState field in Step 2 does not fix this because the plan names no pre-cleanup capture point that populates it.

Step 2 computes changed_files at audit-render time from result.state.workspace_path, but the workspace no longer exists at that point on the success paths. Local landing calls git worktree remove --force .forge/worktrees/{slug} inside _merge_branch (src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:555, invoked from completion.py:1477 during the run), and the PR landing path removes the worktree and then runs git branch -D {branch_name} (src/theforge/coordinator/completion.py:935 and :944). generate_audit_log is only called afterwards, from the terminal writers (src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1499 via _write_story_audit, and src/theforge/cli/shared.py:246 via _write_audit). So for DONE/merged runs — the majority of cost-bearing runs the story is about — the collector finds no workspace and no branch ref and records null, and the Step 2 'fallback to the configured workspace path pattern' resolves to the same deleted directory. AC1, AC3 and AC5 fail for completed runs; only escalated/failed runs (whose worktrees are preserved) would get data.

Step 1 specifies base-branch semantics 'the same as git diff base...HEAD' but the run's base moves: other stories merge into base_branch mid-sprint, and reused worktrees are rebased (_rebase_reused_worktree, src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:1100). A three-dot comparison against the branch name at capture time can therefore differ from the run's actual starting point.

Step 3 bumps both CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION (27) and SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION (8) but does not say the new table must be backfilled for existing indexes; rebuild_from_runs (src/theforge/coordinator/audit_substrate.py:1814) is the path that repopulates from raw_json.

The new CoordinatorState field will not survive a resume: resume_persistence.py serializes explicit blocks (capture_phase_blocks, _preflight_block, _review_progress_block, …) rather than dataclasses.asdict, so an unregistered field is silently dropped.
Binary file insertions/deletions are represented as '-' in git numstat output, which will cause ValueError if parsed directly using int().

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

plan_structured.approach: Capture the run changed-file set while the story worktree and branch still exist, store that immutable snapshot on CoordinatorState, then render it into the final audit record. Persist the same block into raw per-run JSON and project it into a new indexed SQLite join table keyed by run_id and path.

steps.description: Add structured changed-file capture beside the existing review diffstat helper.
steps.details: Keep existing _get_diff_stat(workspace_path, base_branch) behavior for prompts, and add a sibling structured collector that resolves the comparison refs with git at capture time. It should record base_ref as the resolved merge-base sha used for the comparison, not the moving base branch name, and head_ref as the story/worktree HEAD sha. Parse files from git numstat using those resolved refs so the comparison is reproducible later; return null when refs cannot be resolved, otherwise a dict with base_ref, head_ref, and files entries containing path, insertions, deletions. An unchanged comparison returns files: [].

steps.description: Capture changed_files before landing or cleanup and carry it into the canonical per-run audit record.
steps.details: Add CoordinatorState storage for the structured changed_files snapshot. Populate it at a deterministic pre-cleanup seam while the worktree still exists: immediately before successful landing paths call merge/merge-pr cleanup, and on escalated or failed terminal paths before audit writing. generate_audit_log(config, task, result) should serialize the already-captured state.changed_files snapshot rather than recomputing from a possibly deleted workspace. If no snapshot exists, it may fall back to inspecting config.project_root with stored base/head refs or an existing workspace when available; otherwise emit changed_files: null. Emit a top-level changed_files field for every new record: null when unavailable, and {base_ref, head_ref, files: []} when the comparison exists but changed nothing.

steps.description: Project changed files into the audit SQLite index.
steps.details: Bump CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION and SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION. Add an audit_changed_files table with run_id, path, base_ref, head_ref, insertions, deletions, primary key on run_id/path, and an index on path. Extend upsert_run_record(conn, record, ...) to delete then rewrite this table for the run from record['changed_files']['files'] when changed_files is a dict; null or absent changed_files writes no file rows. Ensure the SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump uses the existing rebuild/reindex path, including rebuild_from_runs, so already-indexed records that carry changed_files in raw_json backfill audit_changed_files rows. Add a small query helper or documented SQL path that joins audit_changed_files to audit_records by run_id for per-file spend queries.

steps.description: Keep old records readable with absent file sets distinguishable from empty sets.
steps.details: Add the v27-to-v28 reader migration so migrated old records get changed_files: null, not files: []. Update the schema snapshot fixture for the new top-level field. Ensure schema bootstrap creates the new table on old indexes and any reindex/rebuild path repopulates rows from raw_json when changed_files exists.

steps.description: Add focused tests for audit rendering and indexed file queries.
steps.details: Add a temp-git-repo seam test where changed_files is captured into CoordinatorState before audit rendering and generate_audit_log records base_ref, head_ref, and per-file insertions/deletions for a DONE run. Add an integration test exercising an actual local merge or merge-pr cleanup path where the worktree or branch is removed before _write_story_audit, proving the final audit still contains the stored snapshot. Add a pre-review ESCALATE or DEV-failure result with no reviews. Add substrate tests asserting audit_changed_files rows can be joined back to audit_records by path and match git diff --name-only/numstat for a known run. Add a migration/read test proving v27 raw_json without changed_files loads with changed_files: null while a real empty comparison stores files: [].

criteria_mapping.criterion: A completed run's audit record contains the set of files the run changed against its base ref, with per-file insertions and deletions.
The file set is recorded for runs that terminate before review, including escalated and failed runs.
The recorded base and head refs identify the comparison the file set was derived from.
The file set is queryable per file from the audit index without deserialising every record's raw_json.
A query joining a file to the runs that changed it returns, for a known recent run, the same files that run's commits actually touched.
Records written before this change remain readable, and their absent file set is distinguishable from an empty one.

risks.description: The exact comparison base must match the run's actual comparison point, not a moving base-branch tip chosen later.
risks.mitigation: Resolve and store the merge-base sha at capture time as base_ref plus the final story HEAD sha as head_ref, then parse numstat from those resolved refs.

risks.description: Successful landing paths may delete the worktree or branch before the terminal audit is generated.
risks.mitigation: Capture and store changed_files on CoordinatorState immediately before landing/cleanup, and make audit rendering consume that stored snapshot.

risks.description: Some abnormal termination paths may write audits after the worktree has already disappeared.
risks.mitigation: Represent that as changed_files: null, but capture on normal escalate/fail seams before audit writing so preserved worktrees are indexed.

risks.description: Binary files or unusual filenames can make naive numstat parsing wrong.
risks.mitigation: Parse git numstat with a robust machine-readable mode and define binary insertions/deletions conservatively in tests rather than using formatted --stat output.
